songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy prison set with standout Hard To Handle and crisp China>Rider
ai_show_review.blurb: Features a high‑octane performance of Hard To Handle, Pigpen‑driven blues, and a tight China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue. Phil’s booming bass dominates the mix while Jerry delivers bright lead tones. The concise set runs smoothly despite occasional bass distortion on a few tracks.
ai_show_review.review:
The August 4 1971 prison gig at Terminal Island Correctional Facility captures the Dead in a focused, high‑energy mode. From the opening Truckin’ through a brisk set that never overstays its welcome, the band delivers tight song‑to‑song transitions and a palpable drive fueled by Phil Lesh’s booming bass. Pigpen’s gritty vocals shine on Hard To Handle and Next Time You See Me, while Garcia’s guitar “ticks the chin” with bright leads and occasional humor between tunes. Highlights include an electrifying Hard To Handle that sets the tone, a seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider pair, and crisp renditions of Me & My Uncle and Casey Jones.

The Miller soundboard tape (gd1971-08-04.sbd.miller.95308.sbeok.flac16) presents a mostly clear front mix that places Phil’s bass front‑and‑center, though occasional distortion on Big Boss Man and Sugaree is noticeable. Bill Kreutzmann provides a steady rhythmic foundation, keeping the set grounded as Pigpen’s harmonica and vocals fill the gaps left by the absent keyboards. For listeners seeking an authentic snapshot of the early ’71 prison run, this recording offers excellent clarity and captures the band’s concise yet spirited performance.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with clear front mix and strong bass presence, capturing the set's energy despite minor distortion.

key_highlights: High‑energy Hard To Handle showcases Pigpen’s raw vocals and Phil’s booming bass.
Seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider transition with crisp guitar work.
Concise, tight set typical of the ’71 prison run, highlighted by Me & My Uncle and Next Time You See Me.
Mostly clear soundboard recording; occasional bass distortion on a few tracks.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is bright and “ticks the chin,” delivering solid lead lines throughout and sprinkling humor between songs.
band_performance.Phil: Phil’s bass is fat, funky and often booming in the front mix, driving the momentum despite occasional distortion on a few numbers.
band_performance.Bob: Weir adds high‑note vocal peaks, tells the Yellow Dog story and slips a lyric or two (notably on “Playin’”).
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann keeps a steady pulse, providing a solid rhythmic foundation for the concise set.
